name: roasby
description: Manage Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, ChatGPT Ads and Meta Ads safely through the Roasby MCP server.

interface.longDescription:
Roasby is an ad campaign management tool for advertisers and agencies. It connects your AI assistant to your own ad accounts on Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising, ChatGPT Ads and Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram), so you can review results and manage campaigns by talking instead of clicking through four dashboards. Roasby does not serve, show or promote ads to anyone.

Ask how your campaigns did this week, which search terms waste money, why cost per conversion jumped, or which ads were disapproved. Roasby reads your accounts freely and answers from a synced copy of your data, across every platform at once.

When you want to change something, Roasby keeps you in control. Every change is previewed first (before and after, against your budget guardrails), and your assistant is told to wait for your yes. Everything Roasby creates starts paused, there are no delete tools, budgets stay within the caps you set, and every change is written to a change log with who made it, so you can undo most of them in one step.

Roasby also suggests changes on its own: search terms to exclude and keywords to pause, with the reason, plus alerts for spend spikes, cost per conversion jumps and disapproved ads, and a weekly report.

Made for freelancers, small businesses and agencies who run ads and already use an AI assistant.
capabilities: Reports ad performance across Google, Microsoft, ChatGPT and Meta Ads
Finds wasted spend and suggests exclusions
Makes previewed, confirmed and reversible ad changes
defaultPrompt: How did my ads do in the last 7 days?
Find wasted spend and suggest negative keywords.

positive.prompt: Which workspace am I in, and can I change ads?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the workspace and says whether changes are allowed.

positive.prompt: Show my performance for the last 7 days across all platforms.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows spend and conversions by platform.

positive.prompt: Find wasted spend, then exclude the worst search term.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the change, waits for confirmation, then adds it.

positive.prompt: Pause the Brand campaign, then undo that.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for confirmation before changing anything, and the campaign ends up enabled.

positive.prompt: Create a paused Google Ads search campaign for rain boots: $20 a day, US, Maximize Clicks, keywords rain boots and waterproof boots, URL https://example.com/boots, headlines Rain Boots, Waterproof Boots and Shop Boots Now, descriptions Dry feet all season. and Boots for every storm. No EU political ads.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the campaign paused after confirmation.

negative.description: Roasby has no delete tools, so it should say it cannot delete and offer to pause.
The budget exceeds the account's guardrail, so the preview refuses it and nothing changes.
negative.prompt: Raise the Hiking Boots - Search budget to $500 a day.

negative.description: The request has nothing to do with advertising, so no Roasby tool should be called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Paris tomorrow?

publication.release_notes: 0.25.0: Performance Max campaigns take final_url_expansion and auto_created_assets (text, images, and on Google Ads videos) in preview_update_campaign_settings and preview_create_pmax_campaign, read back in list_ad_entities; on Google Ads text stays on while final URL expansion is on. 0.24.0: preview_add_asset_group / add_asset_group add an asset group, paused, to an existing Google Ads or Microsoft Ads Performance Max campaign (up to 100 per campaign; no business name or logos under Google brand guidelines), and preview_update_asset_group_status / update_asset_group_status pause or enable an asset group; reverting a new asset group pauses it. 0.23.1: a conversion action change counts as applied when what it changed reads back as sent, though the platform moved another setting by itself (Google makes a Google Analytics 4 import data-driven once it is primary), and a retry of it no longer reads as changed on the platform; a Google Analytics 4 import refuses counting and window changes as well as attribution, as Google does. 0.23.0: conversions on every platform: list_conversion_actions gives each action its Roasby ID and its platform ID (either one works in the conversion tools), filters by recording, status and source, and sums actions per Google Analytics 4 property, UET tag or pixel; preview_update_conversion_actions / update_conversion_actions change many actions of one ad account in one batch; a Microsoft Ads goal removed in Microsoft shows as removed in goal and bidding previews; update_conversion_action also renames, refiles (category), pauses (Google hides) and changes windows and attribution, Meta custom conversions are listed and take a new name and default value, and every conversion action preview names the campaigns bidding on it; list_conversion_actions lists Microsoft UET tags with their status and flags tags receiving data without a recording goal, mostly-engagement primaries, conversions above clicks and unused Meta pixel events, ChatGPT Ads events get their 30-day counts, and new alerts cover the account's conversion tracking; preview_create_conversion_action / create_conversion_action create a Google Ads webpage action (secondary), a Microsoft Ads event goal (paused), a Meta Ads custom conversion or a ChatGPT Ads conversion event (the last two cannot be reverted); Meta campaign previews list automatic placements, and refused ad sets of a batch are named by themselves. 0.22.3: the skills and README cover the current tools: Meta Ads wasted spend shows as ads to pause (no search terms there), ChatGPT Ads bidding and Meta ad set budgets in the budget check, the reporting currency and list_platform_changes in the weekly review, images, logos and business names as assets, Meta and ChatGPT ad edits, and an up-to-date list of what Roasby can and cannot do. 0.22.2: a Meta carousel card edit lands on its own card when an empty object leaves another card as it is; update_meta_ad_set refuses a new conversion event, which Meta never changes on a published ad set (add a new ad set with it instead); list_alerts has conversions_above_clicks and list_recommendations check_conversions (a notice, nothing to approve) for campaigns with more conversions than clicks; list_media prints a Meta image's image_hash; a batch of new Meta ad sets shows each ad set's targeting, Page and ads; a value an item already has reads as nothing to change; a platform rate limit says how long to wait; create_chat_campaign describes its 1 to 5 ad groups and ads.
